reviewMethod: Independent visual sweep of all 32 paper pages and scheme pages 1–24, cross-checking each printed part against its own allocation. All question/solution crops inspected before publication; graph checked against both printed functions.
sourceNotes: All ten questions retained: 44 tasks and 380 offered marks. Exam-level choice does not remove practice questions. Q5(a)(i)–(ii) share 15D and Q9(a)(i)–(ii) share 15C; each pair stays together.

Q1(b) explicitly uses ascending powers. Its third term is 45k⁸/x⁶. Q1(b)(ii) credit notes refer to T7; the x⁴ term is the eighth term in ascending order. Its coefficient 120k³ and final k=4 are correct.
Q2(b)(i) is mislabelled (b)(ii) in the detailed scheme; reconcile to the paper and summary. Q2(b)(iii) means log₂(n+1), not log₂(n)+1.
Q3(b) reuses z1 from the previous part in the model solution; here the given root is 2−i, not 11−2i. The resulting a=−4 and b=5 are correct.

Q3(c) drops a factor 4 before √3i and omits division of the angles by 3 in an intermediate line. Its three final roots are correct: modulus 2 and angles π/9, 7π/9, 13π/9. The card explains the correct intermediate formula.
Q4(b)(i) expands −(k²+1)k incorrectly as −k²−k. It must be −k³−k. The card supplies the corrected expansion.
Q6(a) specifically prints 15D (0,5,8,12,15), unlike the general 15D table (0,4,8,12,15). Retain its task-specific numeric bands only for this card. Local minimum confirmed by g″(11/2)=52>0.

Q7(d)(i) writes the growth factor 1.004495498 as the interest rate i. Subtract 1 before expressing it as 0.45%. Q7(d)(ii) uses that rounded monthly rate. Q7(e) requires the least whole year strictly above log(2)/log(1.0675), namely 11; 10.61164 is not equal to 11.
Q8(a)(iii) and Q5(b) use (a)/(b) internally in the model proof; these are working steps, not extra printed tasks. Q8(b)(i) keeps the proof and both roots together under 10D.
Q9(a)(ii) prints −8.14×10 in the exponential substitution; the correct exponent is −0.814×10=−8.14. The final answer 2994 is correct.

Q9(a)(iv) prints 5C (0,2,3,5) but gives Low, Mid and High Partial Credit descriptions. Preserve numeric bands and original wording; the extra Mid description has no distinct numeric award, so no substitute official allocation is invented.

Q9(b)(iii) incorrectly compares rates on intervals separated at t=5, confusing graph height with slope. An attributed NextStepUni graph and valid comparison explain that both populations increase towards 3000, N initially steepens then flattens, while P flattens throughout. Original SEC wording remains visible with an explicit correction.
Q10(b) uses y for |BE| in its working, independent of the y in the later cylinder question. Q10(c)(ii) maximum is at y=4√3 with V″(y)=−12πy<0; the endpoints give zero volume.

A sum of money, €A, is invested in a fund and is withdrawn after t years, where t ∈ ℕ. The money is invested at a fixed APR of 6·75%. Find the least value of t needed so that the investment will amount to more than €2A when it is withdrawn from the fund.
cards.markingNote: The threshold is about 10.61164 years; because t is a whole number and the investment must exceed €2A, the least valid t is 11.
